vedic_reference.note: Taraknath is a popular name in Hinduism, derived from the name of Lord Taraka, who is considered the god of deliverance from all kinds of sufferings. In Hindu mythology, Lord Taraka is a form of Lord Vishnu, who is believed to have the power to save his devotees from all forms of distress and misery. The name Taraknath is thus a reverential invocation to this deity, seeking his blessings for protection and deliverance from suffering.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Taraknath" represents a deep-rooted belief in the power of deities to protect and save their devotees from harm. It exemplifies the importance of faith and devotion in Hindu culture. The name carries a sense of strength and security, instilling confidence and reassurance in those who bear it.
data.spiritual_significance: Taraknath is a name aligned with the divine and the sacred. It embodies the idea of a higher power that is always watching over and protecting its devotees. In spiritual terms, the name signifies the inner strength and fortitude that is derived from faith and devotion. It is a reminder of the ultimate salvation and liberation that awaits those who immerse themselves in the divine.

historical_references.reference: Taraknath was a famous Hindu monk and a Jaina Tirthankara of the 11th century AD. He is believed to have lived during the 11th-12th centuries AD in Bengal, India. Taraknath was a renowned scholar and ascetic, and his teachings and works have had a profound impact on Jainism in Bengal and beyond.

Taraknath is also known as the 'Bengal Tirthankara' because of his prominent role in Jainism in Bengal. He is considered an important figure in the history of Jainism in India, and his teachings and writings continue to be studied and revered by Jains around the world.
historical_references.context: Prominent figure in Jainism in Bengal
